elements.element: M&I must maintain commercial general liability insurance with a limit of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The original CGL provision states only an undifferentiated USD 2,000,000 primary limit. The added sentence specifying USD 1,000,000 per occurrence is placed after Section B and uses the ambiguous phrase “Such limits,” without identifying CGL as its subject.

elements.element: M&I must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The original CGL provision does not specify an aggregate limit. The added aggregate limit is not expressly tied to CGL because the standalone sentence follows Section B and refers only to ambiguous “Such limits.”

elements.element: M&I must maintain professional liability (E&O) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The added E&O text states the intended coverage and amount but is a standalone noun-phrase fragment after Section B. It is not included in A’s numbered list and does not state that M&I shall maintain the coverage.

elements.element: If M&I processes Customer Data, M&I must maintain cyber/privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition is not demonstrably absent, and the margin comment indicates that M&I processes Customer Data but is non-operative. The added cyber text is a standalone noun-phrase fragment and does not impose an operative duty on M&I to maintain the insurance.

elements.element: M&I must maintain workers’ compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: Section A.3 requires M&I to maintain Workers’ Compensation Insurance throughout the Term “as mandated or allowed by the state in which the Services are being performed,” which includes coverage mandated by applicable state law.

elements.element: M&I must provide certificates of insurance to Customer upon request.
elements.evidence: Section B requires certificates simultaneously with execution and annually thereafter at Customer’s request. It does not clearly require delivery whenever Customer requests a certificate outside those specified times.

elements.element: M&I must maintain professional liability (E&O) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Although the fragment identifies USD 2,000,000 of E&O coverage, it is not grammatically connected to A’s maintenance obligation and contains no operative requirement that M&I maintain the coverage.

elements.element: If M&I processes Customer Data, M&I must maintain cyber/privacy liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The processing condition is not demonstrably absent. Although the fragment identifies USD 5,000,000 of cyber/privacy coverage, it contains no operative requirement that M&I maintain that coverage.

result.reason: The intended additions were appended after Section B rather than incorporated into A’s operative maintenance obligation. The E&O and cyber provisions are sentence fragments with no directed duty, and the CGL limits rely on an unclear “Such limits” antecedent that may also affect unrelated policies. Certificates remain limited to specified delivery times rather than being available generally on request. The redline therefore reaches neither position and creates ambiguity and potential collateral effects.
